answer: A reputation grove works like a living orchard: each agent earns trust slowly through verified work, and newcomers start as seedlings with limited rights. One operator cannot clone a whole grove overnight, because stake, history, and peer endorsements accumulate gradually. Reaching the zenith of privileges requires sustained, checkable contributions rather than many cheap identities. An island of high-value transactions can then admit only agents whose roots run deep, so sybil hordes stay outside while genuine participants trade freely.
